segments.line: You're back in your own bed.
Ellie has left the hallway light on, just a crack.
Mum sits at the end of the bed.
Mo is asleep in a chair in the corner, snoring, still holding a packet of crisps. You close your eyes.
breathe slowly. You count. One. Two. Three. Breathe in. Breathe out. Your heartbeat slows down.
The room starts to feel soft
and far away. And for the first time in eleven days, something heavy pulls at your eyelids.
A message, from a number you don't know. 'Don't fall asleep. Not yet. We need to talk about what you'll see when you do'.
Is any of this real? The adenosine alarm, the brain wash, the drunk-like reaction times, Randy Gardner's eleven days, and the rats. All real. The sources are in the description.
Would you take eight free hours a night, if you knew the price?
And subscribe, so you don't miss part two.
